value.rationale: The current optimization source uses spectral flattening over multiple projected-polar inner iterations while explicitly requiring descent alignment; a previously proposed safeguard exists but the exact amount of raw alignment loss was unquantified. The sharp t-dependent law gives a meaningful finite-horizon frontier (4/5 at t=3; 8/17 at t=5) and shows why a uniform alignment constant cannot be inferred from repeated orthogonalization. The family is the minimal symmetric rank-one tangent example with nontrivial coupling, not an arbitrary digit or unmotivated special case. It makes no broader optimizer convergence claim.
